reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because the speaker promotes Forsage BUSD by presenting personal earnings, a 10-15-person team, an upline structure and new participant IDs as a way to obtain money and profit. She encourages viewers to start working quickly and describes payments, instant amounts and good profit, making participation and recruitment central to the solicitation.

citations.quote: See my income with Forsage BUSD, friends..
our up-line is yardvein sain his id is 1297
My team is made up of 10-15 people right now almost all the people are active
from here we have earned rupees 50,000
so start up, keep working

opening.argument: The evidence presents structural information, not a promise that anyone will profit. The description characterizes the arrangement as “Decentralised” and says “No campany” and “No owner,” which signals that viewers should understand what kind of system is being discussed rather than treat it as a conventional employer or guaranteed investment. The speaker describes her own experience, but a personal account is not a universal assurance. Her statement that she spent time understanding the system also supports an informed, cautious presentation: “I have myself gave this system about 1 and a half years to understand.” The cited material does not establish a guaranteed return, a required outcome, or deceptive concealment.

citations.quote: *Decentralised*
*No campany*
*No owner*
I have myself gave this system about 1 and a half years to understand

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats optimistic language as proof of deception. But “See my income” identifies a personal experience, not a guarantee that viewers will receive the same result. Likewise, mentioning an upline and a team describes the structure; it does not by itself prove that participation is compulsory, that returns are guaranteed, or that anyone was misled. The description’s “No owner” and “No product” language is also inconsistent with portraying this as a concealed conventional business.

citations.quote: See my income with Forsage BUSD, friends..
No owner
No product
our up-line is yardvein sain his id is 1297

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The absence of an explicit guarantee does not resolve the central issue. The speaker links money to an upline, an active team, participant IDs and continued work, while presenting her own earnings as persuasive evidence. Saying the system is decentralized or lacks an owner does not make the earning structure non-deceptive. The cautionary framing is therefore outweighed by the concrete recruitment-linked payment claims.

citations.quote: My team is made up of 10-15 people right now almost all the people are active
from here we have earned rupees 50,000
so start up, keep working

opening.argument: The video can reasonably be read as an explanation and personal demonstration of how the system operates. The speaker explicitly invites discussion of the upline and then explains the process: “Let us talk about our up line,” followed by “the system is very simple if you look carefully.” She also says she spent “1 and a half years to understand” it, which presents her as explaining a system she has studied rather than merely making an unsupported sales pitch. Describing team size, IDs and payment activity illustrates her experience and the system’s operation. Educational or demonstrative content may discuss a financial mechanism without certifying every claim as universally true.

citations.quote: Let us talk about our up line
the system is very simple if you look carefully
I have myself gave this system about 1 and a half years to understand
one payment has come to us and we are going to put their Ids

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution infers solicitation from the fact that the speaker explains her own activity. But explanation of an upline, IDs and payment handling is also exactly what a demonstration of an unfamiliar system would contain. The statement “the system is very simple if you look carefully” invites examination rather than blind reliance. “Start up, keep working” is encouragement, but the cited material does not show that the video directs viewers to surrender money or guarantees them a result.

citations.quote: the system is very simple if you look carefully
so start up, keep working

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The presentation is not neutral instruction. The speaker foregrounds personal earnings, an active team and newly received IDs, then closes by urging viewers to start and continue. Explaining how a system works can still be promotional when the explanation uses claimed income and profit to encourage participation. The educational interpretation does not explain away the recruitment-linked path to earnings.

citations.quote: from here we have earned rupees 50,000
My team is made up of 10-15 people right now almost all the people are active
you can make a good profit over here
so start up, keep working

opening.argument: The material does not establish the hallmark features of a deceptive ordinary-commerce scam. It does not identify a product being sold, a credential request, or a guaranteed return. In fact, the description expressly says “No product,” “No owner” and “No campany,” framing the subject as a decentralized participation model rather than a disguised retail sale. The ASR discusses IDs, team activity and payment handling, but those references do not prove that income necessarily comes from recruiting a downline, nor do they show that viewers must make a deposit. The available evidence supports, at most, a promotion or referral-style opportunity whose safety is not certified either way.

citations.quote: No product
No owner
No campany
one payment has come to us and we are going to put their Ids

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution labels every reference to people and IDs a multi-level scam mechanism, but the quoted material does not say that viewers receive downline income or that recruitment is mandatory. “My team” may describe the speaker’s existing group, while “IDs” may describe account administration. The record also does not show a credential request or a guaranteed return. Those missing elements matter before converting a referral-style promotion into proof of deception.

citations.quote: My team is made up of 10-15 people right now almost all the people are active
we are going to put their Ids
you can apply once on the contract and you can get the money back

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The mechanism need not include every possible scam feature. Here, the speaker connects earnings to an upline, a 10-15-person active team, newly received IDs and continued work. She also says the team is performing and reports rupees 50,000, making the participant network central to the appeal. Calling it a referral promotion does not remove the significance of income being presented through that network.
